prompt: A shop offers a ten-percent discount on an item and then adds ten percent to the reduced price. Explain why the result is not the original price, using an item priced at 100 units. Keep your response near 80 words.
text: A 10% discount on an item priced at 100 units reduces the price by 10 units, leaving 90 units. Then adding 10% means adding 10% of the reduced price, not the original price: 10% of 90 is 9 units. The final price is therefore 90 + 9 = 99 units. It is not the original 100 because the discount and increase are calculated from different bases. Percentages are not automatically reversible when applied successively.
